bounded_objective: After the selector-only sparse-surgery refutation, derive an all-depth retained-credit bound whose constants are independent of rarity and which preserves arbitrary terminal cores without reusing internal H-U credit.
method: Use the exact selector entropy decomposition into Jensen-Shannon and pair-splitting terms; retain the raw spectrum of the physical child difference; transfer from H to U with V=H-U; telescope V over the whole restriction tree.
prior_status: Selector-only uniform payment refuted by a genuine sparse bent-surgery family; a data-core or terminal currency was necessary but not isolated in a complete hierarchy ledger.
mathematical_delta: Proved a universal node bound with coefficients 1 and 3/ln2, then telescoped it on arbitrary-depth fresh-selector trees with fully shared terminal data. All internal H-U potentials cancel; only terminal H-U, one raw child-difference entropy packet per node, and physical selector influence remain.

class_extension.previous: Pure selector payment impossible for sparse coherent surgery; constructive tree payments required separated/disjoint cores or a fixed retained terminal core.
class_extension.new: Retained-credit inequality for arbitrary finite changing-core hierarchies with fully overlapping data coordinates, provided selector coordinates are fresh and node-unique.
class_extension.why_it_matters: It removes depth, rarity, terminal bias, and data-overlap dependence from every proved coefficient and isolates one exact aggregate packet instead of an unspecified hierarchy mismatch.

constants.activation_probability: arbitrary dyadic reach weights induced by finite fair-bit restriction trees

verification.limitations: Floating finite checks validate normalization and implementation; the all-parameter theorem is analytic.
